title: 地図に描かれないもの

paragraphs.english: A map of a town can look complete when every street has a clear name and the distances between important buildings are represented consistently on the page. A visitor using it to find a meeting place may reach the correct address without difficulty, yet someone else following the same route may encounter steps that the map does not show. The difference need not mean that either person has misread the symbols; the map may answer one practical question better than another. Knowing where a road leads is not identical to knowing how easily a particular traveler can use it, especially when details of its surface or slope affect the journey. A familiar-looking representation can therefore conceal the decisions about relevance that made it possible to draw in the first place.
paragraphs.translation: 町の地図は、全ての道に明確な名前があり、主要建物間の距離が紙面で一貫して表されていれば、完全に見えることがある。会合場所を探す来訪者は問題なく正しい住所に着けても、同じ経路をたどる別の人は地図にない段差に出会うかもしれない。違いはどちらかが記号を読み違えたことを必ずしも意味せず、地図が一つの実用的な問いに別の問いよりよく答えているのかもしれない。道の行き先を知ることと、特定の旅行者にとっての使いやすさを知ることは同じではなく、表面や勾配の細部が移動に影響する場合は特にそうだ。見慣れた表現は、そもそも描けるようにした、何を重要とみなすかの判断を隠すことがある。

paragraphs.english: This selectivity is not simply a defect that could be removed by adding every available fact, because a page crowded with details might make an urgent route harder to follow. A map becomes useful partly by emphasizing relationships that matter for a purpose and allowing other information to remain in the background. The difficulty arises when this necessary selection is mistaken for a neutral view that suits every user and every task equally well. A delivery driver, a tourist, and a person avoiding stairs may need different features of the same town to be prominent, without disagreeing about where its streets actually lie. The question is which decisions the map supports and which it leaves the user to make with information from elsewhere.
paragraphs.translation: この選択性は利用可能な全事実を加えれば除ける単なる欠陥ではなく、細部で埋まった紙面では急ぎの経路をたどりにくくなるかもしれない。地図は、目的に重要な関係を強調し、他の情報を背景にとどめることでも有用になる。難しさは、この必要な選択を、全ての利用者と作業に同じように合う中立的な見方と取り違える時に生じる。配達員、観光客、階段を避ける人は、道の位置について対立しなくても、同じ町の違う特徴が目立つ必要があるかもしれない。問うべきは、地図がどの判断を支え、どの判断は他の情報を得て利用者が行うのかということだ。

paragraphs.english: A designer could respond by making the map's intended use explicit and offering additional layers that users can consult without losing the basic street pattern. One layer might mark steps and steep sections, while another could show entrances open at particular hours rather than merely placing a building's name at its center. These additions would not guarantee that conditions never change, so the map should also explain when its information was checked and how uncertainty is represented. Users could then distinguish an unmarked obstacle from a route that had actually been checked and found clear, instead of treating every blank space as reassurance. A recently changed public entrance could be marked as temporarily uncertain until a contributor's report had been independently checked against the conditions on the ground. This distinction would tell users where further inquiry was still needed, rather than converting an unanswered question into an apparently settled fact. Feedback would help identify important omissions, provided that corrections were checked rather than accepted solely because they arrived from the most confident contributor.
paragraphs.translation: 設計者は用途を明示し、基本の道の配置を見失わずに参照できる追加の層を用意することで対応できる。一つの層は段差や急勾配を示し、別の層は建物中心に名称を置くだけでなく、特定時間に開く入口を示してもよい。追加情報で状況が変わらないと保証できるわけではないため、最終確認時期と不確かさの表し方も説明すべきだ。利用者は、空白を全て安心材料とせず、未記載の障害物と実際に確認され問題なしとされた経路を区別できる。最近変更した公共の入口は、提供者の報告を独立に現地状況と照合するまで、暫定的に不確かと表示できる。この区別で、未回答の問いを解決済みの事実のようにせず、追加確認がなお必要な箇所を利用者に伝えられる。最も自信のある提供者から来たというだけで受け入れず、修正を確かめる条件で、反応は重要な欠落の発見に役立つ。

paragraphs.english: The result would be neither an exhaustive copy of the town nor a claim that all maps are equally unreliable. It would be a representation whose purpose, limits, and grounds for revision could be understood alongside its useful simplifications. Readers could trust particular features for stated purposes without assuming that everything relevant to their own journey had already been included. Good mapmaking therefore involves responsible selection and explanation, not the impossible elimination of every difference between a place and the image used to navigate it.
paragraphs.translation: 結果は町の網羅的な複製でも、全地図が同じだけ信用できないという主張でもない。それは有用な単純化とともに、目的、限界、修正の根拠を理解できる表現となる。自分の旅に必要な全てが既に含まれると想定せず、明示した用途に沿って特定の特徴を信頼できる。よい地図作りには、場所と移動に用いる像の全ての違いを不可能にも消すことではなく、責任ある選択と説明が含まれる。

paragraphs.english: A fictional design team develops a desk lamp whose damaged parts can be removed with ordinary tools, and advertises this feature as evidence that the product is easy to repair. Unlike a sealed version, the lamp allows an owner to open the outer case without breaking the covering or discarding components that still work. The improvement is real, yet the team's claim becomes less straightforward when an owner opens the case and discovers that the replacement component is no longer available. Another owner can obtain the part but cannot identify which of several similar components caused the fault, because the instructions describe assembly without explaining diagnosis. Both owners have access to the inside, but neither yet has a workable path from a broken object to a functioning one.
paragraphs.translation: 架空の設計班が、損傷部品を普通の工具で取り外せる卓上灯を開発し、その特徴を修理しやすさの証拠として宣伝する。密閉型と違い、その灯具は覆いを壊したり働く部品まで捨てたりせず、所有者が外装を開けられる。改善自体は実在するが、所有者が開けると交換部品がもう入手できないと分かった時、班の主張は単純でなくなる。別の所有者は部品を入手できても、説明書が組立てだけで診断を説明しないため、似た部品のどれが不調原因か分からない。両所有者とも内部にはアクセスできるが、どちらもまだ、壊れた物を動く物に戻す実行可能な道筋を持たない。

paragraphs.english: These difficulties show why repairability cannot be reduced to one physical feature, even when that feature removes an important obstacle present in earlier designs. Successful repair may depend on a sequence of opportunities, including recognizing the fault, locating a suitable part, understanding the procedure, and checking whether the repair has restored the intended function. Opening the case supports some of that sequence, but does not guarantee the other steps or establish that every owner can complete them independently. A label based only on disassembly could therefore give users a misleading impression of the support available after purchase. This does not make the design improvement worthless; it makes the scope of the claim important. The relevant question is what kind of repair the product enables, for whom, and under which continuing conditions.
paragraphs.translation: これらの困難は、以前の設計の重大な障害を取り除く特徴でも、修理可能性を一つの物理的特徴に還元できない理由を示す。修理成功は、不調の特定、適合部品の入手、手順理解、目的の機能が戻ったかの確認など、一連の機会に左右されうる。外装を開けることは一連の一部を支えるが、他の段階を保証せず、全所有者が独力で完了できると確定もしない。従って分解だけに基づく表示は、購入後に得られる支援について利用者に誤解を与えうる。これは設計改善を無価値にするのではなく、主張の範囲を重要にする。問題は、製品が誰のために、どんな継続条件の下で、どの修理を可能にするかである。

paragraphs.english: The team could improve both the lamp and its explanation by testing repairs with people who did not participate in the original design process. Those tests might reveal where an instruction assumes knowledge that an owner lacks, or where naming a component does not help someone distinguish it from another with a similar appearance. The team could then revise the guidance and state how long replacement parts would be supplied, rather than leaving their future availability to the buyer's imagination. Where a repair requires assistance, information about accessible services may be more useful than a claim that everyone should be able to do it alone. A later owner of the same lamp might need the same guidance even if the original purchaser had lost the printed booklet or could no longer explain an earlier repair. Keeping documentation accessible would extend support beyond the first transaction. Supporting repair need not mean requiring every user to become an expert; it can mean making reliable help and suitable materials obtainable.
paragraphs.translation: 元の設計に関わらなかった人と修理を試すことで、班は灯具とその説明の両方を改善できる。試験からは、説明書が所有者にない知識を前提にする箇所や、部品名だけでは似た外見の別部品と区別できない箇所が分かりうる。班は案内を改め、将来の部品入手を購入者の想像任せにせず、交換部品をどれほどの期間供給するか述べられる。修理に支援が必要な場合、誰でも一人でできるはずという主張より、利用できるサービスの情報が有用なこともある。同じ灯具を後に所有する人には、最初の購入者が冊子を失ったり以前の修理を説明できなくなったりしても、同じ案内が必要かもしれない。資料を参照可能に保てば、初回の取引を超えて支援を続けられる。修理を支えることは全利用者に専門家化を求める必要はなく、信頼できる助けと適切な材料を手に入れられるようにすることでもよい。

paragraphs.english: A more responsible description would connect the product's physical features with the information and supply arrangements that make them useful over time. It would also distinguish what the seller can currently demonstrate from what depends on commitments that must continue after the first sale. Buyers could then evaluate repairability without assuming that a removable screw is a promise about every future difficulty or every possible source of damage. The point is to turn an attractive design principle into a usable relationship between an object and the people expected to maintain it. Repairability is thus a supported capacity to act, rather than a property fully captured by the moment when a case first opens.
paragraphs.translation: より責任ある説明は、物理的特徴と、その特徴を長期的に有用にする情報・供給体制とを結ぶ。売手が現在実証できるものと、初回販売後も続ける必要のある約束に依存するものも区別する。購入者は、外せるねじ一つが将来の全ての不調や損傷原因への約束だと思わず、修理可能性を評価できる。狙いは魅力的な設計原則を、物とその手入れを期待される人との利用可能な関係にすることだ。修理可能性は、最初に外装が開く瞬間だけで全て捉えられる性質ではなく、支援された実行能力なのである。

sentences.english: Successful repair may depend on a sequence of opportunities, including recognizing the fault, locating a suitable part, understanding the procedure, and checking whether the repair has restored the intended function.
sentences.translation: 修理成功は、不調の特定、適合部品の入手、手順理解、目的の機能が戻ったかの確認など、一連の機会に左右されうる。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Successful repair may depend on a sequence of opportunities, including recognizing the fault, locating a suitable part, understanding the procedure, and checking whether the repair has restored the intended function.

sentences.english: Opening the case supports some of that sequence, but does not guarantee the other steps or establish that every owner can complete them independently.
sentences.translation: 外装を開けることは一連の一部を支えるが、他の段階を保証せず、全所有者が独力で完了できると確定もしない。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Opening the case supports some of that sequence, but does not guarantee the other steps or establish that every owner can complete them independently.

sentences.english: A label based only on disassembly could therefore give users a misleading impression of the support available after purchase.
sentences.translation: 従って分解だけに基づく表示は、購入後に得られる支援について利用者に誤解を与えうる。
sentences.sourceEnglish: A label based only on disassembly could therefore give users a misleading impression of the support available after purchase.

sentences.english: This does not make the design improvement worthless; it makes the scope of the claim important.
sentences.translation: これは設計改善を無価値にするのではなく、主張の範囲を重要にする。
sentences.sourceEnglish: This does not make the design improvement worthless; it makes the scope of the claim important.

sentences.english: The relevant question is what kind of repair the product enables, for whom, and under which continuing conditions.
sentences.translation: 問題は、製品が誰のために、どんな継続条件の下で、どの修理を可能にするかである。
sentences.sourceEnglish: The relevant question is what kind of repair the product enables, for whom, and under which continuing conditions.

sentences.english: The team could improve both the lamp and its explanation by testing repairs with people who did not participate in the original design process.
sentences.translation: 元の設計に関わらなかった人と修理を試すことで、班は灯具とその説明の両方を改善できる。
sentences.sourceEnglish: The team could improve both the lamp and its explanation by testing repairs with people who did not participate in the original design process.

sentences.english: Those tests might reveal where an instruction assumes knowledge that an owner lacks, or where naming a component does not help someone distinguish it from another with a similar appearance.
sentences.translation: 試験からは、説明書が所有者にない知識を前提にする箇所や、部品名だけでは似た外見の別部品と区別できない箇所が分かりうる。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Those tests might reveal where an instruction assumes knowledge that an owner lacks, or where naming a component does not help someone distinguish it from another with a similar appearance.

sentences.english: The team could then revise the guidance and state how long replacement parts would be supplied, rather than leaving their future availability to the buyer's imagination.
sentences.translation: 班は案内を改め、将来の部品入手を購入者の想像任せにせず、交換部品をどれほどの期間供給するか述べられる。
sentences.sourceEnglish: The team could then revise the guidance and state how long replacement parts would be supplied, rather than leaving their future availability to the buyer's imagination.

sentences.english: Where a repair requires assistance, information about accessible services may be more useful than a claim that everyone should be able to do it alone.
sentences.translation: 修理に支援が必要な場合、誰でも一人でできるはずという主張より、利用できるサービスの情報が有用なこともある。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Where a repair requires assistance, information about accessible services may be more useful than a claim that everyone should be able to do it alone.

sentences.english: A later owner of the same lamp might need the same guidance even if the original purchaser had lost the printed booklet or could no longer explain an earlier repair.
sentences.translation: 同じ灯具を後に所有する人には、最初の購入者が冊子を失ったり以前の修理を説明できなくなったりしても、同じ案内が必要かもしれない。
sentences.sourceEnglish: A later owner of the same lamp might need the same guidance even if the original purchaser had lost the printed booklet or could no longer explain an earlier repair.

sentences.english: Keeping documentation accessible would extend support beyond the first transaction.
sentences.translation: 資料を参照可能に保てば、初回の取引を超えて支援を続けられる。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Keeping documentation accessible would extend support beyond the first transaction.

sentences.english: Supporting repair need not mean requiring every user to become an expert; it can mean making reliable help and suitable materials obtainable.
sentences.translation: 修理を支えることは全利用者に専門家化を求める必要はなく、信頼できる助けと適切な材料を手に入れられるようにすることでもよい。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Supporting repair need not mean requiring every user to become an expert; it can mean making reliable help and suitable materials obtainable.

sentences.english: A more responsible description would connect the product's physical features with the information and supply arrangements that make them useful over time.
sentences.translation: より責任ある説明は、物理的特徴と、その特徴を長期的に有用にする情報・供給体制とを結ぶ。
sentences.sourceEnglish: A more responsible description would connect the product's physical features with the information and supply arrangements that make them useful over time.

sentences.english: It would also distinguish what the seller can currently demonstrate from what depends on commitments that must continue after the first sale.
sentences.translation: 売手が現在実証できるものと、初回販売後も続ける必要のある約束に依存するものも区別する。
sentences.sourceEnglish: It would also distinguish what the seller can currently demonstrate from what depends on commitments that must continue after the first sale.

sentences.english: Buyers could then evaluate repairability without assuming that a removable screw is a promise about every future difficulty or every possible source of damage.
sentences.translation: 購入者は、外せるねじ一つが将来の全ての不調や損傷原因への約束だと思わず、修理可能性を評価できる。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Buyers could then evaluate repairability without assuming that a removable screw is a promise about every future difficulty or every possible source of damage.

sentences.english: The point is to turn an attractive design principle into a usable relationship between an object and the people expected to maintain it.
sentences.translation: 狙いは魅力的な設計原則を、物とその手入れを期待される人との利用可能な関係にすることだ。
sentences.sourceEnglish: The point is to turn an attractive design principle into a usable relationship between an object and the people expected to maintain it.

sentences.english: Repairability is thus a supported capacity to act, rather than a property fully captured by the moment when a case first opens.
sentences.translation: 修理可能性は、最初に外装が開く瞬間だけで全て捉えられる性質ではなく、支援された実行能力なのである。

title: おすすめが育てる好み

paragraphs.english: An imaginary reading service suggests stories similar to those a reader has previously chosen, and describes its recommendations as a convenient reflection of that person's existing interests. For someone looking for more of a familiar genre, the arrangement may work well, reducing the effort needed to locate a promising title among many unfamiliar ones. After several weeks, however, the reader notices that the home page contains fewer kinds of stories than the service's full collection. Choosing from that page produces another record of apparent preference, which the service then uses to offer still more examples of the same kind. The resulting pattern may reflect both what the reader likes and what the interface has made easy to encounter.
paragraphs.translation: 架空の読書サービスが、読者が以前選んだ物語に似たものを薦め、その推薦を既存の関心を便利に映すものと説明する。なじみのジャンルをさらに読みたい人には、多数の未知の作品から有望な題名を探す労力を減らせるので、仕組みはうまく働くかもしれない。しかし数週間後、読者はホーム画面の物語の種類がサービスの全蔵書より少ないと気づく。その画面から選ぶことで、見かけの好みの記録がまた生じ、サービスはそれを使って同種の作品をさらに示す。生じた傾向は、読者の好みと、画面が出会いやすくしたものの両方を映しているかもしれない。

paragraphs.english: This feedback complicates the idea that a recommendation merely reveals an independent preference, without showing that the reader's enjoyment is false or that every personalized suggestion is harmful. A person can genuinely enjoy a selection while having little opportunity to discover whether something outside it would also be rewarding. Repeated choices therefore cannot automatically establish how broad that person's interests would be under a different set of visible options. The issue concerns the interaction between choice and opportunity, not a simple opposition between authentic human taste and artificial influence. Even a thoughtfully arranged shelf guides attention, but a service that learns from responses should recognize that its own arrangement helped produce the evidence it interprets. Otherwise, an initial narrow selection may acquire the appearance of a stable personal identity without ever being compared with meaningful alternatives.
paragraphs.translation: この循環は、読者の楽しさが偽物とか個別推薦が全て有害だとか示すことなく、推薦が独立した好みを示すだけという考えを複雑にする。選択を本当に楽しみつつ、その外の何かにも価値があるか見つける機会は乏しい場合がある。従って選択の反復から、見える候補が違う時にその人の関心がどれほど広いかを自動的に確定はできない。問題は選択と機会の相互作用であり、本物の人間の好みと人工的影響との単純な対立ではない。考えて並べた棚でさえ注意を導くが、反応から学ぶサービスは、自らの配置も解釈対象の証拠を生んだと認めるべきだ。そうしないと、最初の狭い選択が意味のある別候補と一度も比べられず、安定した個人の性質のように見える恐れがある。

paragraphs.english: A more informative design might retain familiar suggestions while giving readers a clear way to request variety, explore a different category, or change the signals used for future recommendations. It could explain why particular titles were shown, without suggesting that one explanation is a complete description of the person receiving them. An unfamiliar suggestion need not be imposed at every visit, but opportunities for exploration should not disappear simply because a reader repeatedly accepted the easiest available choice. A reader might ignore a suggestion because there was no time to read, rather than because the subject itself lacked appeal. A clearly explained and readily accessible control could let the reader explain that difference without being forced to supply a detailed personal account. Silence alone would remain ambiguous evidence about preference rather than a complete answer. The service could also distinguish a request for something similar from a claim that the reader wants nothing else. These are different statements, even when they produce the same click during one particular browsing session.
paragraphs.translation: より情報を与える設計なら、なじみの推薦を残しつつ、多様性の要求、別分類の探索、将来の推薦信号の変更を明確にできる。特定の作品を示す理由を説明しつつ、その説明一つが受け手の人物像全体だとは示唆しないようにできる。毎回未知の推薦を押しつける必要はないが、最も選びやすい候補を繰り返し選んだからといって、探索機会を消すべきではない。推薦を無視するのは、題材に魅力がないからではなく、読む時間がないからかもしれない。明確に説明され容易に使える操作機能なら、個人事情を詳しく説明するよう強いずに、その違いを伝えられる。反応がないことだけでは、好みの完全な答えではなく、曖昧な証拠のままである。サービスは、似たものを求めることと、それ以外を何も望まないという主張も区別できる。一度の閲覧で同じクリックが生じても、この二つは異なる発言である。

paragraphs.english: Evaluating the design would then require more than counting how often recommended items were opened, because opening a title says little by itself about choices that were never made visible. Readers might be asked whether they could find unfamiliar work when they wanted it, or whether the available controls actually changed what appeared on their page. Convenience would remain a legitimate aim, but it would be considered alongside the user's ability to redirect the service and encounter alternatives. The point is not to replace every familiar choice with a surprise, but to keep the relationship between observed behavior and offered possibilities open to examination. Recommendations can support discovery when they help people develop interests rather than quietly presenting the limits of an interface as the limits of a person.
paragraphs.translation: 従って設計の評価には推薦作品が開かれた頻度を数える以上が必要であり、開く行為だけでは見せていない候補についてほとんど分からない。望んだ時に未知の作品を見つけられたか、操作機能で実際に画面の候補が変わったかを読者に尋ねてもよい。便利さは正当な目標であり続けるが、利用者がサービスの方向を変え、別候補に出会える能力と併せて考えることになる。狙いはなじみの選択を全て意外なものに替えることではなく、観測行動と提示される可能性の関係を検討可能に保つことだ。推薦は、画面の限界をひそかに人物の限界として示す代わりに、関心を発展させる助けになる時、発見を支えられる。

options.text: Recommendations can help readers while also shaping the choices later interpreted as preferences. A responsible service should preserve convenience, explain its signals, and support redirection and exploration rather than treating repeated responses within limited options as a complete personal identity.
options.explanation: 便利さを認めつつ、提示が行動を作る循環を考慮し、説明・探索・方向転換の可能性を残す論点を統合する。

options.text: Recommendations simply reveal interests that exist independently of what a service displays. Repeated clicks therefore establish the full range of a reader's taste, making opportunities for unfamiliar work unnecessary once enough familiar items have been opened.
options.explanation: 提示範囲が選択を形作る点を無視し、既に選ばれた行動から関心の全範囲を確定できると誤る。

options.text: Personalized suggestions are inherently harmful because enjoyment produced within an interface is never genuine. A responsible service should replace every familiar title with a surprise and prevent readers from requesting stories similar to earlier favorites.
options.explanation: 楽しさが偽物とも全推薦が有害ともせず、なじみの選択の全面的置換も目的ではない。

paragraphs.english: A listener returns from a small concert and describes a performance as unusually intimate, remembering both the music and the silence shared with the people seated nearby. Later, a recording of the same event allows the listener to hear musical details that passed unnoticed in the room, yet the experience feels different. One response is to call the recording an inferior copy, on the ground that it fails to reproduce everything that made the evening memorable. Another is to claim that the recording improves on the concert because individual notes can be examined repeatedly without distraction from the audience. Both rely on a comparison whose meaning depends on what the listener expects each form to preserve or make possible.
paragraphs.translation: 聞き手が小さな演奏会から帰り、音楽と近くの人々と共有した沈黙を覚えていて、その演奏を珍しく親密だったと語る。後で同じ催しの録音を聞くと、会場で気づかなかった音楽の細部を聞けるが、体験は異なって感じられる。一つの反応は、その晩を印象的にした全てを再現できないという理由で、録音を劣った複製と呼ぶことだ。別の反応は、聴衆に気を散らされず個々の音を繰り返し調べられるので録音は演奏会より優れると主張することだ。どちらも比較に頼るが、その意味は聞き手が各形式に何を残し、何を可能にしてほしいと考えるかに左右される。

paragraphs.english: A concert may offer a shared situation in which attention is shaped by the presence of others and by knowing that the performance is unfolding without the possibility of restarting it. A recording can make another kind of attention possible, allowing a passage to be replayed, compared with another performance, or heard by someone unable to attend the original event. These opportunities are not merely smaller portions of the same experience; they change how the work can be approached. The fact that something is absent does not by itself establish that the remaining form has no distinctive value, just as access to additional detail does not prove superiority for every purpose. Calling one form more authentic therefore requires an explanation of the relationship being valued, rather than an assumption that closeness to the event settles every question.
paragraphs.translation: 演奏会は、他者の存在や、演奏が巻き戻せず進んでいるという認識に注意を左右される、共有の状況を与えうる。録音は、部分の再生や別の演奏との比較、当日来られなかった人の聴取を可能にして、別種の注意を成立させる。これらの機会は同一体験の小さな一部分にすぎないのではなく、作品への接し方を変える。何かが欠けても残る形式に独自の価値がないとそれだけで決まらず、細部を多く知れることも全目的での優越を証明しない。一方を本物らしいと呼ぶには、出来事への近さで全て決まるとの想定ではなく、どの関係を重視するかの説明が要る。

paragraphs.english: For a fictional ensemble preparing a release, this distinction could guide decisions about what the recording should communicate. The musicians might choose to retain some sounds of the room because those sounds help convey the circumstances, while explaining that the listener's position differs from that of any single audience member. Alternatively, they could favor clarity of musical relationships and acknowledge that this priority leaves some features of the shared evening in the background. Neither choice should be presented as an absence of interpretation, since deciding what to emphasize already shapes the version of the event that reaches another listener. Someone studying the piece might welcome a clear passage that a former audience member remembers chiefly through the feeling of the room. Their different reactions need not be inconsistent, because the two listeners may be asking the recording to perform different tasks. A brief note about these aims could help listeners compare the release with their expectations without requiring agreement that one presentation is the best possible account. The question would shift from whether the recording duplicates an entire evening to whether its choices support the experience it claims to offer.
paragraphs.translation: 架空の合奏団が録音作品を発表する場合、この区別は録音が何を伝えるべきかの判断を導ける。奏者は状況を伝えるため会場音を一部残し、同時に聞く位置は一人の観客の位置とは異なると説明してもよい。別案として音楽的関係の明瞭さを重視し、その優先で共有した晩の一部の特徴が背景に退くと認めてもよい。何を強調するかの決定自体が別の聞き手へ届く催しの姿を形作るため、どちらの選択も無解釈として示すべきではない。曲を学ぶ人は、当日の観客が主に会場の感覚を通して覚える部分を、明瞭に聞けると喜ぶかもしれない。二人は録音に異なる役割を求めているかもしれないため、反応が違っても矛盾とは限らない。目的の短い注記で、一つの提示が最良だという一致を求めず、聞き手が作品と期待を比較するのを助けられる。問いは、録音が晩全体を複製するかから、その選択が提供すると称する体験を支えるかへ移る。

paragraphs.english: This approach leaves room for criticism, because a recording may still obscure an important musical relationship or describe itself in ways that its actual presentation does not justify. Purpose provides a basis for evaluation, not an exemption from it, and listeners need not abandon the qualities they value in live performance. They can instead recognize that different forms invite different uses of attention and ask which gains and losses matter for a particular encounter with the work. Both the recording and the original concert may then become related opportunities rather than rivals forced into a single ranking that ignores what each makes possible. Understanding the difference can deepen engagement with both without pretending that either contains everything the other offers.
paragraphs.translation: この方法でも、重要な音楽的関係を不明瞭にしたり実際の提示が正当化しない自己説明をしたりする録音を批判する余地は残る。目的は評価の根拠を与えるのであり免除ではなく、聞き手は実演で大切にする性質を捨てる必要はない。異なる形式は異なる注意の使い方を招くと認め、作品との個別の出会いでどの利得と損失が重要かを問える。録音と元の演奏会の両方は、それぞれの可能性を無視した単一順位へ押し込む競争相手ではなく、関連する機会になりうる。違いを理解すれば、一方が他方の全てを含むと装わずに、両方との関わりを深められる。

paragraphs.english: A fictional student robotics contest gives every team the same kit of components and the same amount of time to build a machine that can complete a short course. The organizers describe the arrangement as fair, because no team is allowed to purchase a faster motor or bring a completed machine from home. When the event begins, some teams immediately divide the work and adapt plans from earlier projects, while others spend much of the available time learning how the parts fit together. The difference may reflect experience rather than a violation of the rules, yet it raises a question about what equal starting conditions were intended to achieve. Identical materials have removed one source of advantage, but they have not made every participant equally prepared to use those materials.
paragraphs.translation: 架空の生徒向けロボット競技会が、短いコースを走破する機体を作るため、全班に同じ部品セットと同じ時間を与える。高速なモーターの購入や自宅の完成機持込みを禁じるため、主催者はこの方式を公平と説明する。開始後、一部の班はすぐ分担して過去の計画を応用し、他班は時間の大半を部品の組合せの学習に使う。違いは規則違反ではなく経験を反映するかもしれないが、平等な開始条件で何を達成する意図だったかが問われる。同じ材料で優位の一要因は除いたが、全参加者に材料を使う同等の準備を与えたわけではない。

paragraphs.english: This does not establish that experienced teams should lose the benefits of practice, or that a fair contest must produce equal scores. A competition may reasonably aim to recognize developed skill, in which case differences in preparation can be relevant to the achievement being assessed. However, an event advertised as an introduction for beginners makes a different promise from one designed to identify the strongest existing teams. Its rules should be examined in relation to that promise, rather than praised simply because their wording applies equally to everyone who enters. The relevant distinction is between treating a rule consistently and ensuring that the opportunities it offers match the stated purpose of the event. Neither concern can automatically replace the other, because arbitrary exceptions can undermine trust even when organizers hope to help a struggling team.
paragraphs.translation: これは経験班が練習の利益を失うべきだとか、公平な競技なら同点になるべきだとかいう結論にはならない。競技が鍛えた技能の評価を目指すのは妥当で、その場合、準備の違いは評価対象の達成に関わりうる。しかし初心者入門と宣伝する催しは、既存の最強班を見つける設計の催しとは異なる約束をしている。規則は、参加者全員に文言が同じく適用されるというだけで褒めず、その約束に照らして検討すべきだ。重要なのは、規則を一貫して扱うことと、規則が与える機会を催しの明示目的に合うようにすることの区別だ。どちらも自動的に他方に代われず、主催者が苦戦する班を助けたくても、場当たり的例外は信頼を損ないうる。

paragraphs.english: If the aim includes meaningful participation by beginners, the organizers could offer a common introductory session before the timed contest and explain which kinds of prior preparation remain allowed. Separate challenges might recognize both advanced performance and improvement during the event, provided that the criteria are announced clearly rather than adjusted after the results become visible. Participants could then understand what each outcome demonstrates, instead of assuming that a single ranking measures every valuable form of learning or cooperation. These changes would not remove every difference in background, and the organizers should not pretend that a brief lesson makes years of experience irrelevant. They could nevertheless reduce a mismatch between the event's invitation and the conditions under which newcomers are asked to perform. Registration information could describe the expected preparation with examples, so that a newcomer could decide whether the event offered an appropriate challenge before committing time to it. Questions raised by prospective participants before the event might also reveal assumptions hidden in apparently simple instructions, such as whether teams were expected to understand a programming concept already. Clarifying those assumptions in advance would improve the invitation without promising identical preparation for everyone. Keeping those conditions explicit also allows experienced participants to see that their achievements are being interpreted under stated criteria rather than discounted without explanation.
paragraphs.translation: 初心者の意味ある参加も目的なら、主催者は時間制競技の前に共通の入門講習を設け、どの事前準備を引き続き認めるか説明できる。結果を見て基準を変えず、明確に事前発表する条件で、別々の課題が高度な性能と当日の上達を両方評価してもよい。参加者は一つの順位が価値ある学習や協力の全てを測ると思わず、各結果が何を示すか理解できる。変更で背景差の全ては除けず、短い講習で長年の経験が無関係になると主催者は装うべきではない。それでも、案内と、新参加者が成果を求められる条件とのずれは減らせる。登録案内で期待する準備を例示すれば、新参加者は時間を費やす前に、適切な挑戦の機会か判断できる。開催前に参加を考える人から出る質問で、プログラミングの概念を既に理解している想定など、一見簡単な指示に隠れた前提も分かりうる。事前にそうした想定を明確にすれば、全員の準備の同一性を約束せず案内を改善できる。条件を明示しておけば、経験者も、自分の達成が理由なく低く扱われず、明示基準で解釈されていると分かる。

paragraphs.english: Fairness therefore involves more than either identical inputs or equal results; it requires an account of what the competition is for. Consistent rules remain important, but their significance depends partly on whether they create the opportunities that the invitation reasonably leads people to expect. A useful evaluation would ask who could participate meaningfully, what the scores represented, and how the stated purposes shaped the design. It would not assume that every unequal result proves unfairness or that one uniform rule settles all questions about opportunity. The goal is a defensible relationship between the event's purpose, its procedures, and the meaning assigned to its results.
paragraphs.translation: 従って公平さは同一の投入条件か同じ結果かだけではなく、何のための競技かという説明を要する。規則の一貫性は重要だが、その意義の一部は案内から合理的に期待する機会を作るかに左右される。有用な評価なら、誰が意味ある参加をできたか、得点が何を表すか、明示目的が設計にどう影響したかを問う。不揃いの結果は全て不公平の証明だとか、統一規則一つで機会への全ての問いが解決するとは考えない。目標は、催しの目的、手順、結果に与える意味の間に、理由を説明できる関係を作ることだ。
